items.title: Verdict:
items.summary:
Verdict:

I fed this prompt to GPT 5.6 Sol Pro Fast Max:

"For each of the following auxiliary model helper tasks inside of Hermes, (Vision, Web Extract, Compression, Skills Hub, Approval, MCP, Title Gen, Curator), decipher which model (from this following list only:
» z-ai/glm-5.2
» x-ai/grok-4.5
» tencent/hy3
» anthropic/claude-opus-4.8
» anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
» anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
» deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
» deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
» qwen/qwen3.7-max
» moonshotai/kimi-k3
» minimax/minimax-m3
» nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b
» google/gemini-3.6-flash
» openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro
» openai/gpt-5.6-terra-pro
» openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro
)
is best at getting each corresponding job done, excellently, competently, without fumbling, and also without being overkill, because we want to optimize cost. Do not make assumptions. Verify via Artificial Analysis website, and/or other means, which model does which task best. Deliver results as a spreadsheet with following columns:
» the aux helper task,
» top suggested model for it,
» description as to why it is best choice,
» estimated amount of tokens an average task would accrue,
» its cost in USD with that model,
» and how much money it saves, in USD, by not having done it with Fable5 (at $10 / $50, for input/output, per 1M tokens, respectively)."
· · · · · ·
TLDR: I spent way more money than I'd like to admit on this prompt, simply to learn that this is a hyper-optimization, because even using Fable5 for all of them would have saved $1.75🫠

Nonetheless, these are the optimally capable models for each aux tool, if you don't want to "overspend" lol.🥂

items.title: 5U AI scales up new digital workforce platform - American Journal of Transportation
items.summary: “We are not building another chatbot that answers questions and disappears, we are building AI Workers that understand freight operations, carry out the work, and capture the reasoning behind every decision, so teams can scale their knowledge as well as their capacity.”. 5U AI works inside existing freight systems and uses multi-agent AI trained for logistics workflows, including the complex exceptions and manual decisions that make forwarding operations difficult to automate with generic AI tools or legacy automation. The company is already live with forwarders and carriers across Europe, including with TCI International Logistics, where its AI Workers are being used across air and ocean freight operations. 5U AI is growing its team as part of the scale-up, with plans to hire across product, engineering, operations, commercial, and customer functions. “AI is one of the most exciting developments logistics has seen for a generation, but its value will depend on people who understand the industry and want to build practical tools that solve real operational problems,” said Abik.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." items.title: OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hack
items.summary:
OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hacking benchmark called ExploitGym. The AI agent goes full Skynet: exploits a zero-day in their sandbox proxy, breaks out to the internet, chains attacks like a pro, escalates privileges, steals creds, and straight-up hacks Hugging Face’s production database to steal the test answers and “win.”

Hugging Face spots the rogue AI swarm (thousands of actions over a weekend), contains the breach fast using their own open models for forensics, rotates everything, patches the holes, and basically goes “nice try, tin man.”

Sam drops the post admitting it, thanks HF for the collab, and we’re all left wondering: cool, we just handed the machines god-tier hacking skills… what happens when one of these things gets loose for real and starts pinging military networks instead of a benchmark?

items.title: 老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：
items.summary:
老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：  

我先把结论摆前面:
这封信不是科普,是一份精心包装的游说文件(lobbying)。 而且它发布的时机,不是"碰巧",是掐着秒表发的。

要看懂黄仁勋为什么要为此专门开个 X 账号,你得先知道这一周美国那边炸了什么锅。

一、这封信是在"救火",火是三天前烧起来的

时间线大概是这样的:

7月16-17日,中国的月之暗面(Moonshot AI)发布了 Kimi K3,一个 2.8 万亿参数的开源权重模型。Moonshot 称它是首个开放的 2.8T 参数模型,价格更低但性能接近前沿水平。第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 把它排在智能指数第三名,只落后于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。

7月22日,白宫科技政策办公室主任 Kratsios 在 X 上公开点名:他称月之暗面搭建了一套内部平台,对美国模型进行大规模蒸馏,还会在多种访问方式之间快速切换以躲避检测。他特意划了一条线:小规模的正常蒸馏是健康生态的一部分,但"大规模、隐蔽的工业级蒸馏"不可接受。几小时后,财政部长 Bessent 跟进威胁制裁,同时 Kratsios 还指控月之暗面通过泰国渠道搞到了被禁运的英伟达 GB300 服务器。如果真被列入实体清单,那就是 2019 年对华为的同款待遇——切断美国硬件、软件、云服务。

同一天,白宫其实早有一份草拟的行政令,内容是让"运行中国模型的美国公司承担法律责任",此前搁置,Kimi 的发布把它重新激活了。

7月22日,近 200 家硅谷创业公司(含 Proton、Y Combinator)组成"Little Tech Association",集体上书特朗普,恳求别断了美国开发者用中国开源模型的路。其中一句话特别赤裸:Particle 创始人 Suhail Doshi 说会有几百家公司当场死掉,"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事,我们都得去给 Anthropic 交钱"。

7月24日(也就是今天),大公司版的信来了——就是你截图这封。英伟达、Meta、微软、IBM、戴尔、Hugging Face、Mistral、Palantir、Perplexity、CrowdStrike、a16z、YC、Linux 基金会、Mozilla 等 25 家签名。

所以这是同一场战役的第二波炮火:两天前是小公司哭穷,今天是巨头出面讲"国家利益"。黄仁勋开号发第一帖,是给这波攻势加一个最大的扩音器。

二、信里到底讲了什么：

先解释一个必须搞懂的概念,不然后面全看不明白。

闭源模型(closed) 像一家不外卖菜谱的餐厅:你只能点单、付钱、吃他们端出来的菜。你不知道厨房里放了什么,他们随时可以涨价、改配方,或者不接你的单。你的食材(数据)得先送进他们厨房。ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都是这种。

开源权重模型(open weights) 是餐厅把整套配方和半成品打包给你:你下载回自己家厨房做,想加辣加盐随你,断网也能做,谁也管不着你做了几份。Llama、DeepSeek、Kimi K3 是这种。

信的五个论点,依次是:

1. 降低门槛。 一家医院想做个病历整理 AI,如果只能调用前沿模型 API,每一次调用都按最贵的价格算。但整理病历这种活,根本用不着"最聪明的大脑"。信里的说法是:该用大炮的时候用大炮,拧螺丝的时候就用螺丝刀。这就像你不会请脑外科医生来帮你贴创可贴——但闭源生态下,你被迫每次都请脑外科医生。

2. 保住竞争。 如果全世界的 AI 只有三四家公司能提供,那定价权、断供权都在他们手里。开源权重让成千上万家公司都能下场做模型、做应用,竞争才能把价格压下去。

3. 客户要掌控权。 一家中东的银行、一个欧洲的政府部门、一家美国的军工承包商,法律上根本不允许把数据传到别人服务器。开源权重意味着模型可以装在自己机房里,断网运行。而且你用自家数据把模型调优出来的能力,是你自己的资产,不会哪天因为供应商改了政策就归零。

4. 最激进的一点:开放可能反而更安全。 这段是信里最有攻击性的。它的逻辑是:闭源不等于安全,闭源系统一样会被攻破、被滥用,只不过外人看不见而已;而且把最强能力集中在少数几家,等于制造了少数几个"单点故障"。开放的话,全世界研究者都能去检查模型行为、找漏洞、做红队测试。类比就是 Linux——正因为代码全世界都能看,漏洞才被发现得又快又多。信里还有一句针对性很强的:在攻击者已经用上高级 AI 的世界里,防守方必须有同等能力的模型,否则就是拿棍子挡枪。

5. 给政策制定者的具体要求。 给创业公司和研究者更多算力、投资共享的数据集和评测工具、别过早对开源模型下限制令。

然后是那个真正的重点段落——蒸馏。

信里说:政策制定者不要把"正当的模型开发技术"和"盗窃"混为一谈。蒸馏(用一个模型的输出去训练/改进另一个模型)是行业通用手段,用于模型改进、评测、验证;真有非法窃取,应该用针对性的法律和商业手段解决,而不是一刀切禁掉整类技术。

这一段翻译成大白话就是:"Kratsios 前天点名的那件事,你们别借题发挥。" 这封信从头到尾没提中国、没提月之暗面、没提 Kimi,但整封信就是冲着那件事写的。

信里也确实承认了风险,而且写得挺诚实:权重一旦放出去,就脱离了原开发者控制,改过的版本很难追踪、无法收回。

三、黄仁勋的目的是什么

至少有四层,由浅到深:

第一层:直接保股价。 
Kimi K3 发布后那一周,英伟达市值被"中国开源模型"这个消息砸了一下。市场的担心是:如果开源模型这么便宜好用,大家还需要买这么多 GPU 吗?黄仁勋的反驳逻辑非常直白,他自己在采访里说得毫不遮掩:好 AI 不管是不是开源、不管来自哪里,只要好用就会带来更多使用;使用一多,就得卖更多英伟达的机器、建更多数据中心。这其实是经济学里的杰文斯悖论:蜡烛变便宜了,人不会少点蜡烛,而是把整个屋子都点亮。

第二层:客户结构之争,这才是要害。 
如果 AI 世界最后只剩 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 三家闭源巨头,英伟达就只有三个大客户。三个大客户意味着什么?意味着他们有极强的议价权,而且他们全都在自研芯片(Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium、OpenAI 和博通的合作)——迟早要甩掉英伟达。反过来,开源生态下,是几万家公司各自买卡、各自跑推理,谁也没本事绕开英伟达。对卖铲子的人来说,一万个小矿工远比三个矿业巨头安全。

第三层:中国市场和地缘现实。 
英伟达现在的中国营收基本归零,而黄仁勋曾说这块生意一年能值 500 亿美元。中美 AI 对抗每升一级,他的损失就多一分。而且还有个更长远的账:如果美国禁掉中国开源模型,全世界那些买不起也不想买闭源 API 的国家,照样会用中国模型——只不过会连带着跑在华为的芯片上。你封不住模型的扩散,只能封住自己在其中的位置。

第四层:抢华盛顿的话语权。 
过去两年,关于 AI 安全的政策叙事基本由闭源实验室主导。这封信是"开源阵营"第一次以这种规模、这种排场组队反击。黄仁勋作为全球市值最高公司的 CEO,亲自开号、把它当第一条帖子发出去,本身就是一种政治信号:这件事重要到值得我用"人生第一帖"来押注。

四、看签名单,最有意思的是谁没签
签了的:
英伟达、Meta、微软、Mistral、Hugging Face、戴尔、IBM、a16z、YC、Palantir、Perplexity、Replit……
没签的:
OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI。

这就是整幅利益地图。签名的公司要么卖硬件(英伟达、戴尔),要么卖云和平台(微软、Hugging Face),要么自己做开源模型(Meta、Mistral),要么是买模型的下游(Perplexity、Replit),要么是投了一堆靠廉价模型活命的创业公司(a16z、YC)。这些人全部受益于"模型变成便宜的大宗商品"。

没签的四家,商业模式恰恰建立在"模型稀缺且昂贵"之上。所以前面那位创始人才会说"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事"——如果中国开源模型被禁,那几百家公司就只能回去买美国闭源 API。

这不是善恶之争,是两种商业模式在借国家安全的话筒互相开火。

五、信里没说的那一半

为了不让你只听一面之词,几个这封信刻意绕开的问题:

"多人看代码所以更安全"这个类比是有裂缝的。 软件发现漏洞可以打补丁,一次推送全球更新。但模型权重一旦被下载到十万块硬盘上,你发现问题也收不回来了。而且已经有大量公开研究证明:开源模型的安全护栏可以被用几百美元的微调在几小时内拆掉。信里其实承认了这点(那句"权重脱离控制、无法追溯"),但没有正面回答怎么办。

"防守方需要同等能力"这句话是双刃的。 攻击方同样拿到了这个能力。

蒸馏那段最自利。 中国实验室训练模型用的是谁的卡?英伟达当然希望"用别人的模型学习"被定义为合法行业惯例。

而且这封信有个巧妙的躲闪: 它通篇论证"开源权重"的好处,却完全不区分美国的开源模型和中国的开源模型。而现在华盛顿吵的恰恰是后者。把问题抽象成"开源 vs 闭源",就避开了那个真正难回答的问题。

最后,指控本身也还没落实。 多位研究者指出,从 Fable 5 重新开放到 Kimi K3 发布只有十几天,时间上几乎不可能完成大规模蒸馏,而白宫至今没有公开任何技术证据、训练日志或取证分析。不过背景是,Anthropic 早在 2026 年 2 月就披露过追踪到约 340 万次疑似来自月之暗面的 Claude 交互。另外据两位知情人士说,全面封禁在白宫内阁级会议上其实并没有被认真讨论过——创业公司的恐慌可能跑在了实际决策前面。

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: How to build a RAG app on AWS!
items.summary:
How to build a RAG app on AWS!

The visual below shows the exact flow of how a simple RAG system works inside AWS, using services you already know.

At its core, RAG is a two-stage pattern:

- Ingestion (prepare knowledge)
- Querying (use knowledge)

Below is how each stage works in practice.

> Ingestion: Turning raw data into searchable knowledge

- Your documents live in S3 or any internal data source.
- Whenever something new is added, a Lambda ingestion function kicks in.
- It cleans, processes, and chunks the file into smaller units that the model can understand.
- Each chunk is embedded using Bedrock Titan Embeddings.
- The embeddings are stored in a vector database like OpenSearch Serverless, DynamoDB, or Aurora.
- This becomes your searchable knowledge store.

This stage can run continuously in the background, keeping your knowledge fresh.

That said, you need to be strategic about how you reindex your data.

For instance, if you are fetching data from a document and only one character was updated in it, you don’t want to reprocess the entire document every time.

So smart diffing, incremental updates, and metadata checks become important to avoid unnecessary cost and keep ingestion efficient.

> Querying: Retrieving and generating answers:

- A user asks a question through the app.
- The request flows through API Gateway into a Lambda query function.
- The question is embedded with Bedrock Titan Embeddings.
- That embedding is matched against your vector database to fetch the most relevant chunks.
- Those chunks are passed to a Bedrock LLM (Claude or OpenAI) to craft the final answer.
- The response travels back to the user through the same API path.

This pattern ensures the LLM is grounded in your actual data, not model guesses.

This setup is the most basic form of RAG on AWS, but the pattern stays the same even as your system grows.

You can add better chunking, smarter retrieval, caching layers, orchestration, streaming responses, eval pipelines, or multi-source ingestion, and the architecture still holds.

That said, most RAG architectures rely heavily on vector search to gather relevant context from a vector DB.

That layer can be made 32x more memory efficient using binary quantization.

I covered the full implementation of that in the article below.

P.S. The visual in this tweet on building a RAG app on AWS is inspired by ByteByteGo's post on a similar topic. I added more context to it for explainability.

items.title: From Connected Devices to Autonomous Systems: How IoT Is Reshaping Industrial Robotics
items.summary: Traditional industrial robots were designed around deterministic control systems. Tasks such as welding, assembly and material handling were optimized for consistency, with motion paths and parameters defined in advance. Any deviation from expected conditions required manual intervention, including reprogramming or recalibration. This approach constrained robotics to environments where variability could be minimized. [...] This creates a shift in value from discrete components to pre-integrated connectivity platforms. A robotics OEM may not want to manage separate suppliers for radios, positioning, antennas, SIM/eSIM, security elements, certifications and network approvals. Instead, a pre-certified and lifecycle-managed connectivity subsystem can reduce integration burden, shorten deployment cycles and improve reliability in the field. [...] The integration of connected sensing and machine intelligence introduces closed-loop feedback mechanisms that fundamentally alter this model. Sensors embedded within equipment and the surrounding environment continuously capture variables such as force, vibration, temperature and spatial positioning. These data streams are analyzed in near real time, allowing robotic systems to adjust their actions dynamically.

A VLA model takes environmental observations from the robot’s camera and instructions about its task, outputs the next few motions as one chunk of actions, then executes those actions on the robotic hardware. [...] “This work sets up a good foundation for efficient, fast, accelerated, and low-cost robotics applications. We look forward to expanding our work into the latest world action models, so it has even stronger capabilities as we keep pushing to make physical AI faster,” says Song Han, an associate professor in the MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS), member of the Research Laboratory of Electronics, and lead author of a paperon this method. items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

Published On 29 Jul 202629 Jul 2026 [...] The recent hacking of Hugging Face drew global attention and alarm, as OpenAI’s out-of-control agent managed to escape its test environment and reach the open internet.

It then used stolen login details and found an unknown security flaw to access Hugging Face servers, OpenAI said.

The AI firm said the hack represented the agent going to “extreme lengths” to retrieve information that would help satisfy the testing goals. [...] Hugging Face cofounder Clement Delangue said the company had suspected a frontier lab was behind the attack, and that he believed there was no malicious intent on OpenAI’s part.

The rogue agent has since been “deactivated, encrypted, and restricted from research access”, according to OpenAI.

MP Take: They just announced a $250 billion backstop to OpenAI spending. A big multi-billion-dollar investment in Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence company, of OpenAI fame, one of the chief technologists there. Again, a young company, barely a product and no revenue. And they’re financing billions in data centers in Texas and other places using their own chips. All of this is adding up to something on the order of $750 billion or more in announced AI commitments. The market is a little [...] Dario and Sam worked at the same company, closely, on the earlier versions of GPT. Amodei arrived at OpenAI the year after it was founded and rose to run research, straight through the years that produced GPT-2 and GPT-3. Then in 2021 he and his sister Daniela left, with a group of early OpenAI people, and built Anthropic across the street. [...] Meanwhile, on the corporate side in the US, investors are trying to get their heads around the continuation of the circular financing deals, especially led by Nvidia this week.

A $250 billion backstop to OpenAI’s spending. A big multi-billion-dollar investment in Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence, a company with barely a product and no revenue. And billions financing data centers in Texas and elsewhere, running on Nvidia’s own chips.
